paragraphs: PrimeEnergy Resources Corporation (the "Company") was organized in March 1973, under the laws of the State of Delaware. We are an independent oil and natural gas company engaged in acquiring, developing, and producing oil and natural gas. We presently own producing and non-producing properties located primarily in Texas, and Oklahoma. All of our oil and gas properties and interests are located in the United States. Through our subsidiaries Prime Operating Company and EOWS Midland Company, we act as operator and provide well-servicing support operations for many of the onshore oil and gas wells we operate, as well as for third parties. We are also active in the acquisition of producing oil and gas properties through joint ventures with industry partners. In addition, we own a 12.5% overriding royalty interest in over 30,000 acres in the state of West Virginia. We are currently not receiving revenue from this asset, as development has not begun. In addition, through a wholly owned offshore company, we own a currently idle 60-mile-long pipeline offshore on the shallow shelf of Texas.

PrimeEnergy files or furnishes annual, quarterly, and current reports, proxy statements, and other documents with the SEC under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the "Exchange Act"). The SEC maintains a website (www.sec.gov) that contains reports, proxy and information statements, and other information regarding issuers, including PrimeEnergy, that file electronically with the SEC.

The Company makes available, free of charge, through its website (www.primeenergy.com) its Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K and, if applicable, amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) of the Exchange Act as soon as reasonably practicable after it electronically files such material with, or furnishes it to, the SEC. In addition to the reports filed or furnished with the SEC, the Company publicly discloses information from time to time in its press releases. Such information, including information posted on or connected to the Company's website, is not a part of, or incorporated by reference in, this Report or any other document the Company files with or furnishes to the SEC.
Information contained on the Company's website is not part of or incorporated into this Report or any other filings with the SEC.

The Company's goal is to responsibly develop its oil and gas reserves, predominantly through horizontal drilling. Our strategy includes targeting reservoirs with high initial production rates and cash flow as well as targeting reservoirs with lower initial production rates but with higher expected return on investment. We believe that with today's technology, horizontal development of our reserves provides superior economic results as compared to vertical development, by delivering higher production rates through greater contact and stimulation of a larger volume of reservoir rock while minimizing the surface footprint required to develop those same reserves.

Maintaining a strong balance sheet and ample liquidity are key components of our business strategy. In 2026, we plan to continue our focus on preserving financial flexibility and liquidity as we manage the risks facing our industry. Our capital budget for the year is reflective of current commodity prices and has been established based on an expectation of available cash flows, with any cash flow deficiencies expected to be funded by borrowings under our revolving credit facility. As we have done historically to preserve or enhance liquidity, we may adjust our capital program throughout the year, divest non-strategic assets, or enter into strategic joint ventures.

Horizontal development of our leasehold acreage has continued at a fast pace, particularly in West Texas, where in 2025 we participated with Double Eagle, and Vital in the drilling and completion of 23 new horizontal wells targeting the Wolfcamp and Spraberry producing intervals. There are at least six pay intervals ("benches") being developed in the Midland Basin, from the deeper Wolfcamp "D" up through the shallower Middle Spraberry. The economic variability from one area to another and from one well to another depends on geologic properties (thickness, porosity, permeability, and hydrocarbon maturity), lateral length, stimulation, and oil price, as well as the economies of scale and therefore cost advantages often achieved by the more active operators. Under our leasehold acreage in the Midland Basin, several of these benches have either never been tested, or not yet developed, however, near our acreage, some of these benches have just recently been aggressively developed. We estimate that our acreage in Reagan, Upton, and Martin counties has the potential for as many as 100 drilling locations for these benches that we believe will likely be drilled in the next several years. In particular, under our large acreage position in Reagan County, only the Wolfcamp "A" and "B" intervals have been developed so far, along with a one-well test of the Wolfcamp "D" on one block.

In 2023, the Company completed 35 horizontal wells operated by five operators: 32 of these are located in West Texas and three in Oklahoma. In total, including the cost of facilities, the Company invested approximately $96 million, 99% of which was for wells in West Texas where we have been developing various proven pay intervals in the Wolfcamp and Spraberry formations. Below is a recap of our horizontal development activity in 2023.

In Reagan County, Texas we participated with Hibernia Energy II (Now Civitas) in ten 2-mile-long horizontals carrying 25% interest and investing $25.6 million. These ten wells on our "Brynn" tract began production in April 2023. Also in Reagan County in 2023, we participated with DE IV, LLC (Double Eagle) in 15 horizontals and invested approximately $34.8 million: five of these were 2-mile-long laterals on the "Prime East" tract that were placed on production in May 2023, in which we have nearly 50% interest, another six 2-mile-long laterals on the "Studley AV" tract that were brought on production in December 2023 in which we have 7% interest, and four 2.5-mile laterals on the "Studley CKO" tract that were completed in December 2023 in which we have 20% interest. These 25 Reagan County wells were all completed in 2023.

In Upton County, Texas, we participated for 50% interest in two 3-mile-long horizontals operated by Apache. These were brought into production in October 2023 and required an investment of approximately $17 million through completion of the wells and central facilities. In Martin County, Texas in 2023, we participated with ConocoPhillips for 20.8% interest in five 2.5-mile-long horizontal laterals, investing approximately $12 million. These five were completed and brought online in September 2023. Also in 2023, in Oklahoma, we joined Ovintiv USA, Inc. in the drilling of three 3-mile-long horizontals located in Canadian County with 2% interest and invested approximately $645,000.

In 2024, the Company invested $113 million in 48 horizontals in West Texas: 47 of these are located in Reagan County and one is located in Upton County. In Reagan County, the Company joined Double Eagle in drilling and completing 33 new horizontal wells: on the "Honey RF" tract we completed 12 horizontals each being two-mile-long laterals, and participated with 50% interest investing $37 million; on the "Prime West" tract we have 50% interest in six wells and invested $20.5 million; on both the "Kramer" and "O'Bannion" tracts we participated in six horizontals, each with an average 8.3% interest and we invested approximately $7.8 million; and on the "Pink Floyd" tract we have less than 1% interest in two wells in which we invested approximately $174,900; and on our"Studley AV" tract we participated with Double eagle in testing the Wolfcamp "D" interval; in this well we have about 6.3% interest and invested approximately $600,000. Also in Reagan County, we participated with Civitas in 14 horizontal wells on the "Christi" tract, carrying an average of 39% interest and investing roughly $46.7 million. Also in 2024, in Upton County, we participated with Pioneer Natural Resources in one 2-mile-long horizontal with 3.94% interest, investing approximately $425,800. Of these 48 wells, 32 are 2-mile-long laterals, 14 are 2.5-mile-long laterals, and two are 3-mile-long laterals.

In addition to this activity, in June of 2024, we participated with Apache in the drilling of six additional 3-mile-long laterals in Upton County on our "Mt. Moran" tract. Three of these wells were completed in late December 2024 and three were completed in January of 2025. All six new "Mt. Moran" wells are producing as of April 1, 2025. In these six Mt. Moran wells, the Company has an average of 51.16% interest and invested approximately $36.3 million. In addition, in November of 2024, in Reagan County, we participated with Double Eagle in 15 "OG" horizontal wells: eight are 2.5-mile-long laterals, and seven are 2-mile-long laterals. In each of these 15 "OG" wells the Company has approximately 23% interest and in total invested roughly $23 million. Each of these 15 horizontals were on production as of May 2025 and the Company has invested approximately $59.3 million in these additional 21 horizontal wells.

In early March 2025, Ovintiv Mid-Continent spud two "Jennifer 1407" wells in Canadian County, Oklahoma; we participated for approximately 3.14% interest and invested $405,000, these wells were completed in May 2025. In the second and third quarters of 2025, we participated in fifteen new horizontals in the Midland Basin of West Texas: these 15 wells are operated by Double Eagle on our "Full House" tract in Reagan County in which the Company participated with approximately 27% interest and invested approximately $30.1 million. In addition to the Reagan County activity, the Company participated in eight "Horseshoe" wells in Midland County with Vital Energy. Drilling activity with these wells began in the second quarter and the wells were put on production during the fourth quarter of 2025. The company has an average of 8.2% interest in these eight wells and invested approximately $5.4 million. We also participated with Devon Energy Production on two "Evelyn" wells in Kingfisher County, Oklahoma; we participated with approximately 9.95% interest and $1.4 million. These wells were drilled in July 2025 and completed November 2025. In total in these 27 wells, we invested approximately $37.3 million.

The Company's horizontal development activities in the last three years, can be summarized as follows: in 2023 we invested $96 million in 35 horizontals, in 2024 we invested $113 million in 48 horizontals, and in 2025, we invested $96 million in 48 horizontals. Therefore, in total, since January 2023 and through 2025, the Company will have invested roughly $305 million in horizontal development, primarily in the Midland Basin of West Texas. It is also noteworthy, that since the start of our horizontal development activities in 2012 the Company has invested over $435 million in horizontal drilling in the Midland Basin of West Texas, and $47 million in Oklahoma, predominantly in the Scoop/Stack Play.

headings: General Risk Factors

The prices of oil, NGL and gas are highly volatile. A sustained decline in these commodity prices could materially and adversely affect the Company's business, financial condition and results of operations.
Concerns over general economic, business or industry conditions may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, liquidity and financial condition.
We have substantial capital requirements, and we may not be able to obtain needed financing on satisfactory terms, if at all.
Negative public perception regarding us and/or our industry could have an adverse effect on our operations.
We may not be insured against all of the operating risks to which we are exposed.
Terrorist activities and the potential for military and other actions could adversely affect our business.
Our ability to sell our natural gas and oil production could be materially harmed if we fail to obtain adequate services such as transportation and processing.
Competition in our industry is intense, and many of our competitors have substantially greater financial and technological resources than we do, which could adversely affect our competitive position.
The loss of key personnel could adversely affect our ability to operate.
A failure of technology systems, data breach or cyber incident could materially affect our operations.
Risks Related to our Business
The shut-in of our wells could negatively impact our production, liquidity, and, ultimately, our operations, results, and performance.
Drilling natural gas and oil wells is a high-risk activity.

The Company's expectations for future drilling activities will be realized over several years, making them susceptible to uncertainties that could materially alter the occurrence or timing of such activities.
Our future performance depends on our ability to find or acquire additional natural gas and oil reserves that are economically recoverable.
The borrowing base under our revolving credit facility may be reduced in light of recent commodity price declines, which could limit us in the future.
We face a variety of hazards and risks that could cause substantial financial losses.
The nature of the Company's assets and production operations may impact the environment or cause environmental contamination, which could result in material liabilities to the Company.
We have limited control over the activities on properties we do not operate.
We may have hedging arrangements that expose us to risk of financial loss and limit the benefit to us of increases in prices for natural gas and oil.
Legal and Regulatory Risks
The Company's operations are subject to a number of risks arising out of concerns regarding the threat of climate change.
paragraphs: Our revenues, operating results, financial condition and ability to borrow funds or obtain additional capital depend substantially on prevailing prices for natural gas and oil. Lower commodity prices may reduce the amount of natural gas and oil that we can produce economically. Natural gas prices, based on the twelve-month average of the first of the month Henry Hub index price, were $3.39 per MMBTU in 2025 as compared to $2.13 per MMBTU in 2024, and have averaged $3.64 per MMBTU for the first four months of 2026. Oil prices, based on West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Light Sweet Crude first-of-the-month prices, averaged $65.34 per barrel in 2025 as compared to $75.48 per barrel in 2024, and in the first three months of 2026, the first-of-the-month price has averaged $65.72 per barrel.

Any substantial or extended decline in future natural gas or crude oil prices would have a material adverse effect on our future business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, liquidity or ability to finance planned capital expenditures and commitments. Furthermore, substantial, extended decreases in natural gas and crude oil prices may cause us to delay or postpone a significant portion of our exploration, development and exploitation projects or may render such projects uneconomic, which may result in significant downward adjustments to our estimated proved reserves and could negatively impact our ability to borrow and cost of capital and our ability to access capital markets, increase our costs under our revolving credit facility, and limit our ability to execute aspects of our business plans.

Prices for natural gas and oil are subject to wide fluctuations in response to relatively minor changes in the supply of and demand for natural gas and oil, market uncertainty and a variety of additional factors that are beyond our control. These factors include:
the level of consumer product demand; the domestic and foreign supply of natural gas and oil
weather conditions and natural disasters;
political conditions in natural gas and oil producing regions, including the Middle East, Russia, Africa and South America;

paragraphs: MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

The following discussion is intended to assist you in understanding our results of operations and our present financial condition. Our Consolidated Financial Statements and the accompanying Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements included elsewhere in this Report contains additional information that should be referred to when reviewing this material. Our subsidiaries are listed in Note 1 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.

We are an independent oil and natural gas company engaged in acquiring, developing, and producing oil and natural gas. We presently own producing and non-producing properties located primarily in Texas, and Oklahoma. In addition, we own a substantial amount of well servicing equipment. All of our oil and gas properties and interests are located in the United States. Assets in our principal focus areas include mature properties with long-lived reserves and significant development opportunities as well as newer properties with development and exploration potential. We believe our balanced portfolio of assets and our ongoing hedging program position us well for both the current commodity price environment and future potential upside as we develop our attractive resource opportunities. Our primary sources of liquidity are cash generated from our operations and our credit facility.

We attempt to assume the position of operator in all acquisitions of producing properties and will continue to evaluate prospects for leasehold acquisitions and for exploration and development operations in areas in which we own interests. We continue to actively pursue the acquisition of producing properties. To diversify and broaden our asset base, we will consider acquiring the assets or stock in other entities and companies in the oil and gas business. Our main objective in making any such acquisitions will be to acquire income producing assets to build stockholder value through consistent growth in our oil and gas reserve base on a cost-efficient basis.

Our cash flows depend on many factors, including the price of oil and gas, the success of our acquisition and drilling activities and the operational performance of our producing properties. We use derivative instruments to manage our commodity price risk. This practice may prevent us from receiving the full advantage of any increases in oil and gas prices above the maximum fixed amount specified in the derivative agreements and subjects us to the credit risk of the counterparties to such agreements. Since all our derivative contracts are accounted for under mark-to-market accounting, we expect continued volatility in gains and losses on mark-to-market derivative contracts in our consolidated statement of operations as changes occur in the NYMEX price indices.

Our financial results depend on many factors, particularly the price of natural gas and crude oil and our ability to market our production on economically attractive terms. Commodity prices are affected by many factors outside of our control, including changes in market supply and demand, which are impacted by weather conditions, pipeline capacity constraints, inventory storage levels, basis differentials and other factors. In addition, our realized prices are further impacted by our derivative and hedging activities. We derive our revenue and cash flow principally from the sale of oil, natural gas and NGLs. As a result, our revenues are determined, to a large degree, by prevailing prices for crude oil, natural gas and NGLs. We sell our oil and natural gas on the open market at prevailing market prices or through forward delivery contracts. Because some of our operations are located outside major markets, we are directly impacted by regional prices regardless of Henry Hub, WTI or other major market pricing. The market price for oil, natural gas and NGLs is dictated by supply and demand; consequently, we cannot accurately predict or control the price we may receive for our oil, natural gas and NGLs. Index prices for oil, natural gas, and NGLs have been volatile in recent years and consequently cannot determine with any degree of certainty what effect increases or decreases in these prices will have on our capital program, production volumes or revenues.

Proved oil and gas reserves directly impact financial accounting estimates, including depreciation, depletion and amortization. Proved reserves represent estimated quantities of natural gas, crude oil, condensate, and natural gas liquids that geological and engineering data demonstrate, with reasonable certainty, to be recoverable in future years from known reservoirs under economic and operating conditions existing at the time the estimates were made. The process of estimating quantities of proved oil and gas reserves is very complex, requiring significant subjective decisions in the evaluation of all available geological, engineering and economic data for each reservoir. The data for a given reservoir may also change substantially over time as a result of numerous factors including, but not limited to, additional development activity, evolving production history and continual reassessment of the viability of production under varying economic conditions. Consequently, material revisions (upward or downward) to existing reserve estimates may occur from time to time.

The quantities of estimated proved oil and gas reserves are a significant component of our calculation of depletion expense and revisions in such estimates may alter the rate of future expense. Holding all other factors constant, if reserves were revised upward or downward, earnings would increase or decrease respectively. Depreciation, depletion and amortization of the cost of proved oil and gas properties are calculated using the unit-of-production method. The reserve base used to calculate depletion, depreciation or amortization is the sum of proved developed reserves and proved undeveloped reserves for leasehold acquisition costs and the cost to acquire proved properties. The reserve base includes only proved developed reserves for lease and well equipment costs, which include development costs and successful exploration drilling costs. Estimated future dismantlement, restoration and abandonment costs, net of salvage values, are taken into account.

The Company has significant obligations to remove tangible equipment and restore land at the end of oil and gas production operations. The Company's removal and restoration obligations are primarily associated with plugging and abandoning wells. Estimating the future restoration and removal costs is difficult and requires management to make estimates and judgments. Asset removal technologies and costs are constantly changing, as are regulatory, political, environmental, safety, and public relations considerations. ARO associated with retiring tangible long-lived assets is recognized as a liability in the period in which the legal obligation is incurred and becomes determinable. The liability is offset by a corresponding increase in the underlying asset. The ARO liability reflects the estimated present value of the amount of dismantlement, removal, site reclamation, and similar activities associated with the Company's oil and gas properties. The Company utilizes current retirement costs to estimate the expected cash outflows for retirement obligations. Inherent in the present value calculation are numerous assumptions and judgments including the ultimate settlement amounts, inflation factors, credit-adjusted discount rates, timing of settlement, and changes in the legal, regulatory, environmental, and political environments. Accretion expense is recognized over time as the discounted liability is accreted to its expected settlement value

Our primary sources of liquidity are cash generated from our operations, through our producing oil and gas properties, field services business and sales of acreage, and available capacity under our revolving credit facility.
Net cash provided by operating activities for the year ended December 31, 2025, was $96.7 million compared to $115.9 million in the prior year.

Excluding the effects of significant unforeseen expenses or other income, our cash flow from operations fluctuates primarily because of variations in oil and gas production and prices or changes in working capital accounts. Our oil and gas production will vary based on actual well performance but may be curtailed due to factors beyond our control.

Our realized oil and gas prices vary due to world political events, supply and demand of products, product storage levels, and weather patterns. We sell the majority of our production at spot market prices. Accordingly, product price volatility will affect our cash flow from operations. To mitigate price volatility, we sometimes lock in prices for some portion of our production through the use of derivatives.

If our exploratory drilling results in significant new discoveries, we will have to expend additional capital to finance the completion, development, and potential additional opportunities generated by our success. We believe that, because of the additional reserves resulting from the successful wells and our record of reserve growth in recent years, we will be able to access sufficient additional capital through bank financing.

paragraphs: PrimeEnergy Resources Corporation (the "Company") 於 1973 年 3 月 根據 美國 特拉華州 法律 組織 成立。本公司 為 獨立 的 油氣 公司，從事 油氣 的 取得、開發 與 生產。目前，本公司 擁有 位於 德克薩斯州 與 奧克拉荷馬州 的 生產中 與 未生產 的 資產。本公司 所有 的 油氣 資產 與權益 均 位於 美國。透過 我們 的 子公司 Prime Operating Company 與 EOWS Midland Company，本公司 當作 操作者，並為 我們 所經營 的 多數 地面 油氣井 提供 井服務 支援 操作，同時 也 為 第三方 提供 服務。本公司 也 活躍 於 透過 與 行業 合作夥伴 的 聯合 資源 計畫 取得 生產中 的 油氣 資產。此外，本公司 擁有 西維吉尼亞州 超過 30,000 英畝 的 12.5% 預先 優先 優先權 權益。目前，本公司 尚未 從 此 資產 獲得 收入，因 開發 尚未 開始。此外，透過 本公司 全資 的 海上 公司，本公司 擁有 位於 德克薩斯州 淺水 河牀 的 60 英里 長 的 空閒 管線。
PrimeEnergy 向 美國 證券交易委員會 (SEC) 提交 或 提供 年度、季度、現況 報告、股東 指示書，以及 其他 文件，根據 1934 年 證券交易法 (the "Exchange Act")。SEC 保有 網站 (www.sec.gov)，其中 包含 報告、股東 指示書 與 信息 說明書，以及其他 有關 發行人的 信息，包括 PrimeEnergy，其 提交 文件 給 SEC。

本公司 透過 其 網站 (www.primeenergy.com) 免費 提供 其 根據 10-K 表格 所提交 的 年度 報告、根據 10-Q 表格 所提交 的 季度 報告、根據 8-K 表格 所提交 的 現況 報告，以及 若適用，這些 報告 的 修改 版本，於 本公司 電子 提交 這些 文件 給 SEC 或 提供 給 SEC 後，儘可能 早日 提供。除了 向 SEC 提交 的 報告 之外，本公司 會 不時 在 媒體 聲明 中 公開 信息。這些 信息，包括 網站 上 或 與 網站 有關 的 信息，並非 本報告 或 本公司 提交 或 提供 給 SEC 的 其他 文件 的 一部分，亦未 被 引用 為 本報告 或 其他 文件 的 一部分。
本公司 網站 上 的 信息 並非 本報告 或 本公司 提交 給 SEC 的 其他 文件 的 一部分。

本公司 的 目標 是 責任地 發展 其 油氣 資源，主要 透過 水平 鑽井。我們 的 策略 包括 靶向 具有 高 初始 產率 與 現金 流 的 油氣 層，以及 靶向 具有 較低 初始 產率 但 高 預期 投資 回報 的 油氣 層。我們 相信，透過 現代 技術，我們 資源 的 水平 開發 提供 更佳 的 經濟 效果，相較於 垂直 開發，透過 更大的 接觸 與 刺激 更大的 油氣 層體積，同時 減少 開發 同樣 資源 所需 的 地面 足跡。

維持 強健 的 資產 表與 足夠 的 流動性 是 我們 商業 策略 的 關鍵 組成 部分。2026 年，我們 計畫 繼續 聚焦 於 保持 財務 靈活性 與 流動性，以 管理 我們 行業 所面臨 的 風險。我們 的 資本 預算 為 當前 原料 價格 所反映，並根據 可用 現金 流 的 預期 建立，任何 現金 流 不足 預期 將 透過 我們 循環 信用 線 的 借款 資金。如同 我們 歷史 上 維持 或 提升 流動性 所做 的，我們 可能 在 本年度 調整 我們 的 資本 計畫，處置 非戰略 資產，或 參與 戰略 聯合 資源 計畫。

我們 的 租賃 留置 英畝數 的 水平 開發 繼續 以 快速 速度 進行，特別是在 西德克薩斯州，2025 年 我們 與 Double Eagle，Vital 合作，在 狼營 (Wolfcamp) 與 斯普拉伯裏 (Spraberry) 產層 鑽探 與 完井 了 23 個 新 水平 井。在 米德蘭 基礎 (Midland Basin) 至少 有 六個 產層 ("benches") 正在 開發，從 更深 的 狼營 "D" 繼續 到 更淺 的 中部 斯普拉伯裏。不同 地區 或 不同 井 的 經濟 變異 性 取決 於 地質 特性 (厚度、孔隙度、滲透率、烴類 成熟度)、水平 長度、刺激 處理、油價，以及 更活躍 的 操作者 所 得到 的 節省 成本 和 節省 效率。在 我們 的 租賃 留置 英畝數 中，米德蘭 基礎 的 這些 產層 中，有些 未曾 經過 測試，或 尚未 開發，然而，在 我們 的 留置 英畝數 周邊，一些 這些 產層 最近 已經 被 豪華 開發。我們 估計，我們 在 雷根 (Reagan)、尤頓 (Upton) 和 馬丁 (Martin) 縣 的 留置 英畝數 有 可能 達到 100 個 鑽探 位置，我們 相信 這些 位置 將 在 接下來 的 幾年 被 鑽探。特別 是，在 我們 在 雷根 縣 的 大 留置 英畝數 中，目前 只有 狼營 "A" 和 "B" 產層 已經 開發，以及 在 一個 塊 地區 的 狼營 "D" 進行 了一個 一井 測試。
2023 年，本公司 完成 35 個 水平 井，由 五家 操作者 管理：其中 32 個 位於 西德克薩斯州，三個 位於 奧克拉荷馬州。總計，包括設施 成本，本公司 投資 約 96 百萬 美元，其中 99% 用於 西德克薩斯州 的 井，我們 在 狼營 和 斯普拉伯裏 產層 開發 各種 已證實 的 產層。以下是 我們 2023 年 水平 開發 活動 的 總結。

在德州的雷根縣，我們與Hibernia Energy II（現為Civitas）合作，參與了十口長2英里的水平井，持有25%權益並投資25.6百萬美元。這些位於我們「Brynn」地塊的十口井於2023年4月開始生產。此外，在2023年雷根縣，我們與DE IV, LLC（Double Eagle）合作，參與了15口水平井，投資約34.8百萬美元：其中五口為長2英里的水平井，位於「Prime East」地塊，於2023年5月開始生產，我們持有近50%權益；另外六口為長2英里的水平井，位於「Studley AV」地塊，於2023年12月開始生產，我們持有7%權益；以及四口長2.5英里的水平井，位於「Studley CKO」地塊，於2023年12月完成，我們持有20%權益。這些25口雷根縣的井均於2023年完成。

在德州的Upton縣，我們持有50%權益，參與了兩口長3英里的水平井，由Apache經營。這些井於2023年10月開始生產，完成井及中央設施的投資約為17百萬美元。在2023年德州的Martin縣，我們與ConocoPhillips合作，持有20.8%權益，參與了五口長2.5英里的水平井，投資約12百萬美元。這五口井於2023年9月完成並開始生產。此外，在2023年奧克拉荷馬州，我們與Ovintiv USA, Inc.合作，在加拿大縣鑽探了三口長3英里的水平井，持有2%權益，投資約645,000美元。

在2024年，本公司在西德州投資113百萬美元，用於48口水平井：其中47口位於雷根縣，1口位於Upton縣。在雷根縣，本公司與Double Eagle合作鑽探並完成33口新的水平井：在「Honey RF」地塊，我們完成12口水平井，每口為長2英里的水平井，並持有50%權益，投資37百萬美元；在「Prime West」地塊，我們持有50%權益，投資20.5百萬美元；在「Kramer」和「O'Bannion」地塊，我們參與了6口水平井，每口平均持有8.3%權益，投資約7.8百萬美元；在「Pink Floyd」地塊，我們持有少於1%權益的兩口井，投資約174,900美元；在「Studley AV」地塊，我們與Double Eagle合作測試Wolfcamp「D」區間；在這口井中，我們持有約6.3%權益，投資約600,000美元。此外，在雷根縣，我們與Civitas合作，在「Christi」地塊參與了14口水平井，平均持有39%權益，投資約46.7百萬美元。此外，在2024年Upton縣，我們與Pioneer Natural Resources合作，在一口長2英里的水平井中持有3.94%權益，投資約425,800美元。這48口井中，32口為長2英里的水平井，14口為長2.5英里的水平井，2口為長3英里的水平井。

除了上述活動，於2024年6月，我們與Apache合作，在Upton縣的「Mt. Moran」地塊鑽探了六口長3英里的水平井。其中三口於2024年底完成，三口於2025年1月完成。截至2025年4月1日，這六口「Mt. Moran」井均已開始生產。在這六口Mt. Moran井中，本公司持有平均51.16%權益，投資約36.3百萬美元。此外，於2024年11月，在雷根縣，我們與Double Eagle合作，在15口「OG」水平井中參與：其中八口為長2.5英里的水平井，七口為長2英里的水平井。在這15口「OG」井中，本公司持有約23%權益，總投資約23百萬美元。這些15口水平井於2025年5月開始生產，本公司在這21口新增水平井中總投資約59.3百萬美元。

在2025年3月初，Ovintiv Mid-Continent在奧克拉荷馬州加拿大縣鑽探了兩口「Jennifer 1407」井；我們持有約3.14%權益，投資405,000美元，這些井於2025年5月完成。在2025年第二及第三季，我們參與了西德州Midland Basin的15口新水平井：這些15口井由Double Eagle經營，位於我們「Full House」地塊的雷根縣，本公司持有約27%權益，投資約30.1百萬美元。除了雷根縣的活動，本公司還參與了Midland縣的八口「Horseshoe」井，與Vital Energy合作。這些井的鑽探活動於第二季開始，於2025年第四季開始生產。本公司在這八口井中持有平均8.2%權益，投資約5.4百萬美元。我們還與Devon Energy Production合作，在奧克拉荷馬州Kingfisher縣的兩口「Evelyn」井中參與，持有約9.95%權益，投資1.4百萬美元。這些井於2025年7月鑽探，於2025年11月完成。總計在這27口井中，我們投資約37.3百萬美元。

本公司在過去三年的水平開發活動可歸納如下：2023年投資96百萬美元於35口水平井，2024年投資113百萬美元於48口水平井，2025年投資96百萬美元於48口水平井。因此，自2023年1月起至2025年，本公司總計投資約305百萬美元於水平開發，主要位於西德州Midland Basin。值得注意的是，自2012年本公司開始水平開發活動以來，本公司已在西德州Midland Basin投資超過435百萬美元於水平鑽探，並在奧克拉荷馬州投資47百萬美元，主要集中在Scoop/Stack Play。

paragraphs: 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論分析
以下討論旨在協助您瞭解我們的營運成果與目前財務狀況。我們的合併財務報表及附屬的合併財務報表附註，包含更多資訊，當您審閱此資料時應參考。我們的子公司名單請參閱合併財務報表附註第 1 項。

本公司為一獨立之油氣公司，從事取得、開發與生產油氣。目前本公司擁有位於德州與奧克拉荷馬州之生產中與未生產之油氣資產，並擁有大量之井服務設備。所有本公司之油氣資產與權益均位於美國。本公司主要關注領域之資產包括成熟之油氣資產，具長壽命之儲量與重大開發潛力，以及較新之油氣資產，具開發與探勘潛力。本公司相信，我們平衡之資產組合與持續之避險計畫，使我們在現行油氣價格環境與未來潛在上漲中，均能處於有利地位。本公司主要流動性來源為營運所產生之現金及信用融資。
我們試圖在所有生產中資產之取得中擔任操作者，並持續評估租賃取得與探勘開發作業之潛在機會。我們持續積極尋求取得生產中資產。為分散與拓展資產基礎，我們將考慮取得其他油氣公司之資產或股票。我們在進行任何此類取得時之主要目標為取得能產生收入之資產，以透過成本效益方式持續增長本公司油氣儲量基礎，進而提升股東價值。
本公司之現金流取決於許多因素，包括油氣價格、取得與鑽探活動之成效以及生產中資產之營運表現。我們使用衍生工具來管理油氣價格風險。此做法可能使我們無法獲得油氣價格超過衍生合約中所規定之最高固定金額之全部好處，並使我們面臨衍生合約對手方之信用風險。由於所有衍生合約均按市價計價，因此我們預期在合併營運損益表中，因紐約商品交易所（NYMEX）價格指數變動而產生之獲利與損失將持續出現波動。

本公司之財務表現取決於許多因素，特別是天然氣與原油價格以及本公司以經濟上有利條件行銷生產之能力。油氣價格受許多我們無法控制之因素影響，包括市場供需變動，而市場供需變動受天氣條件、管線容量限制、庫存量、價差及其他因素影響。此外，我們之實際價格亦進一步受到衍生與避險活動之影響。本公司之收入與現金流主要來自油、天然氣與液化天然氣（NGLs）之銷售。因此，本公司之收入在很大程度上取決於原油、天然氣與液化天然氣之現行價格。本公司以公開市場價格或透過遠期交割合約銷售油與天然氣。由於部分營運位於主要市場之外，因此我們直接受到區域價格影響，而與亨利中心（Henry Hub）、西德克薩斯 Intermediate（WTI）或其他主要市場價格無關。油、天然氣與液化天然氣之市場價格由供需決定；因此，我們無法準確預測或控制我們可能獲得之油、天然氣與液化天然氣之價格。油、天然氣與液化天然氣之指數價格在近年來表現波動，因此無法確定價格上漲或下跌對我們之資本計畫、生產量或收入之影響。

已證實之油氣儲量直接影響財務會計之估計，包括折舊、耗竭與攤銷。已證實之儲量代表根據地質與工程資料，以合理確定性顯示未來年份可從已知儲層中，在估計時之經濟與營運條件下回收之天然氣、原油、凝析油與液化天然氣之估算數量。估算已證實之油氣儲量數量之過程非常複雜，需在評估所有可用地質、工程與經濟資料時做出重大主觀判斷。某一儲層之資料亦可能因多種因素而隨時間大幅變動，包括但不限於額外開發活動、生產歷史之演進以及持續評估在不同經濟條件下生產之可行性。因此，現有儲量估計可能不時出現重大修正（上漲或下跌）。

估算之已證實油氣儲量數量為本公司計算耗竭費用之重要組成部分，而此等估算之修正可能改變未來費用之速率。假設其他因素不變，若儲量修正為上漲或下跌，則獲利將相應增加或減少。已證實油氣資產之折舊、耗竭與攤銷係以單位生產法計算。用以計算折舊、折舊或攤銷之儲量基礎為租賃取得成本與取得已證實資產之成本之已證實已開發儲量與已證實未開發儲量總和。該儲量基礎對於租賃與井設備成本僅包括已證實已開發儲量，其包含開發成本與成功探勘鑽井成本。估算之未來拆卸、復原與放棄成本，扣除殘值後，已納入考量。

本公司有重大義務在油氣生產作業結束時移除實體設備並復原土地。本公司之移除與復原義務主要與封井與放棄井有關。預估未來復原與移除成本困難，需管理階層做出估計與判斷。資產移除技術與成本持續變動，同時相關之法規、政治、環境、安全與公共關係考量亦持續變動。與退休實體長期資產相關之ARO（Asset Retirement Obligation）應於法律義務產生且可確定之期間認列為負債，並同時使相關資產增加相同金額。ARO負債反映本公司油氣財產相關之拆卸、移除、場地復原及類似活動之預估現值。本公司利用現行退休成本來估計退休義務之預期現金流出。現值計算中內含許多假設與判斷，包括最終結算金額、通貨膨脹因素、信用調整後折現率、結算時間點，以及法律、法規、環境與政治環境之變動。隨時間推移，認列累計費用以將折現負債累計至預期結算價值
本公司主要流動性來源為營運活動所產生之現金，透過生產油氣財產、場地服務業務及出售土地，以及現金循環信用融資之可用容量。

排除重大未預見費用或其他收入之影響，本公司營運活動之現金流變動主要因油氣生產與價格之變動，或營運週轉項目之變動。本公司油氣生產將因實際井之表現而有所變動，但可能因超出本公司控制之因素而受到限制。
本公司實現之油氣價格因世界政治事件、產品供應與需求、產品庫存量及天氣模式而有所變動。本公司將大多數生產以現貨市場價格銷售。因此，產品價格波動將影響本公司營運活動之現金流。為緩解價格波動，本公司有時會透過衍生工具鎖定部分生產之價格。
若本公司探勘鑽井結果導致重大新發現，將需支出額外資本以資助完成、開發，以及因成功而產生之潛在額外機會。本公司認為，因成功鑽井所產生之額外儲備，以及本公司近年備轉增長之紀錄，將能取得足夠額外資本，透過銀行融資實現。

headings: 一般風險因素
石油、NGL 及天然氣價格波動極大。這些商品價格持續下跌可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
對總體經濟、商業或產業狀況的擔憂可能會對我們的營運成果、流動性及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
我們有相當大的資金需求，我們可能無法以滿意的條件取得所需融資，甚至可能無法取得。
對我們及/或我們產業的負面公眾觀感可能會對我們的營運造成不利影響。
我們可能無法對我們所面臨的營運風險進行全部保險。
恐怖攻擊活動及軍事及其他行動的潛在可能可能會對我們的業務造成不利影響。
如果我們未能取得足夠的相關服務，如運輸及處理，我們銷售天然氣及石油產出的能力可能會受到重大影響。
我們產業的競爭非常激烈，許多競爭對手擁有遠較我們為多的財務與科技資源，這可能會對我們的競爭地位產生不利影響。
關鍵人員的流失可能會對我們的營運能力產生不利影響。
技術系統失敗、資料外洩或網路事件可能會對我們的營運產生重大影響。
與本公司業務相關的風險
我們油井的停工可能會對我們的產量、流動性，以及最終的營運、結果與表現產生負面影響。
鑽探天然氣與石油井是一項高風險活動。
本公司對未來鑽探活動的預期將在數年內實現，使其容易受到不確定性因素的影響，這些因素可能會重大改變這些活動的發生或時間。
我們未來的表現取決於我們能否找到或取得額外的天然氣與石油儲量，且這些儲量必須具有經濟價值可回收。
我們的循環信貸融資之借款基礎可能因近期商品價格下跌而降低，這可能會限制我們未來的資金運用。
我們面臨多種風險與危害，這些可能導致重大財務損失。
本公司資產與生產運營的性質可能影響環境或導致環境污染，這可能會使本公司產生重大負債。
我們對不直接經營之不動產的活動沒有完全控制權。
我們可能有避險安排，這些安排可能使我們面臨財務損失的風險，並限制我們因天然氣與石油價格上漲而獲得的利益。
法律與法規風險
本公司運營面臨多種風險，這些風險源自對氣候變遷威脅的關注。
paragraphs: 本公司營業收入、營運成果、財務狀況及取得融資或追加資本之能力， substantially depend on 當前天然氣與石油之價格。若商品價格下跌，可能降低本公司經濟上可生產之天然氣與石油數量。根據亨利指數（Henry Hub index）每月第一日價格之十二個月平均，2025 年天然氣價格為每 MMBTU 3.39 美元，較 2024 年之每 MMBTU 2.13 美元為高，且 2026 年前四個月之平均價格為每 MMBTU 3.64 美元。石油價格根據西德州中質原油（West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Light Sweet Crude）每月第一日價格計算，2025 年平均為每桶 65.34 美元，較 2024 年之每桶 75.48 美元為低，且 2026 年前三個月之每月第一日價格平均為每桶 65.72 美元。

未來天然氣或原油價格若出現大幅或持續下跌，將對本公司未來業務、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流、流動性或籌資預計資本支出及承諾產生重大不利影響。此外，天然氣與原油價格若出現大幅或持續下跌，可能導致本公司延後或擱置大量探勘、開發及開採計畫，或使這些計畫變得不經濟，這可能會導致本公司預估之已證儲量出現顯著下降，並可能影響本公司取得融資與資金成本的能力，以及影響本公司進入資本市場的能力，提高本公司週轉信用貸款之成本，並限制本公司執行業務計畫之能力。
天然氣與石油之價格會因天然氣與石油之供給與需求出現相對微小變化、市場不確定性及多種其他因素而大幅波動，而這些因素皆超出本公司之控制範圍。這些因素包括：
消費者產品之需求程度；天然氣與石油之國內與國際供給量
天氣條件及自然災害；
天然氣與石油生產地區之政治條件，包括中東、俄羅斯、非洲及南美洲
